description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis, logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to approximately 10⁴) and the accuracy (ACC, %) on the y-axis (linear scale from 30% to 55%) for five different model configurations: Base (black solid line with circle markers), FT (blue dashed line with downward triangle markers), IKE (red dash-dotted line with upward triangle markers), MEND (brown dotted line with diamond markers), and ROME (green solid line with square markers). The Base model remains nearly flat across the x-axis, starting at approximately 29% ACC at co-occurrence 1 and slightly increasing to about 32% at 10⁴. FT begins at ~32% and rises gradually to ~38%. IKE starts at ~33% and increases to ~41%. MEND begins at ~36%, rises to ~45% around 10², then plateaus near 45.5%. ROME shows the steepest growth, starting at ~44% and climbing to ~58% at 10⁴, consistently outperforming all other methods across the full range of co-occurrence numbers.
